Vivek,

Thanks — as we move toward signature this week the execs need a concise MAP checkpoint focused on inference economics and performance.

Ask: can you share the latest end-to-end benchmarking snapshot (latency p50/p95, throughput tokens/sec at target batch sizes, and expected cost per 1M tokens) and a short list of tuning actions you’ll run this week that could materially change numbers?

Context: our procurement team (Aaron) wants to confirm the SLA and that the Dedicated plan can hit our 95th percentile latency target of <= 220ms for 8k seq loads before we finalize the reserved commitment.

Please include a proposed internal/exec signoff date and any remaining blockers. If it helps, include the MAP PDF we’ve been working from so we can align on owners/dates.

Sara Palmer
SVP Product, MediLink Systems

Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — performance benchmarking & close timeline

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Attached are the benchmarking artifacts and an updated MAP snapshot. Summary up front:

- Benchmark snapshot (run: 2027-09-13, infra: Dedicated A100 pool, 8k sequence simulated workload):
  - p50 latency: 98 ms
  - p95 latency: 198 ms
  - steady-state throughput: 2,100 tokens/sec per GPU (avg across 5 runs)
  - cost estimate: ~$8.10 per 1M tokens (hosted-equivalent baseline; Dedicated reserved pricing will reduce unit cost ~18% per your commitment tier)

- Observations: p95 is within your 220ms target on the A100 pool with current batching (batch size 8, dynamic batching window 40ms). We see occasional 1–2% spikes at tail when cold KV cache hits coincide with long prompts.

- Tuning actions we’ll run this week (impact & owner):
  1) KV cache warmup prefetch (high impact — reduces cold-start p95): Rafael Mendes — 9/15 EOD
  2) Batch window tightening from 40ms -> 25ms (latency tradeoff vs throughput; small effect on p50) — Neha Kapoor — 9/15 noon
  3) Quantization profile test (int8 + selective fp16 for attention kernels) — Launched as A/B canary; expected throughput +12% — Rafael Mendes — 9/16
  4) Prefix caching for common prompts (customer-provided top-100 prompts) — Monica Patel — 9/17

Planned deliverables this week: latest CSV with token-level traces (attached: llm-latency-run-20270913.csv), an updated MAP PDF (MAP-v2-MediLink.pdf), and perf screenshots. We will run the KV warmup + batch window change first; Rafael will run a targeted canary across two machines to measure p95 delta before any fleet-wide change.

Proposed signoff timeline: internal exec review on 9/17, final procurement and signature 9/20 if tuning results confirm p95 <= 220ms on Dedicated. If the canary shows a >5% improvement in p95, we’ll accelerate.

Action items (quick):
- Rafael Mendes: implement KV prefetch canary + quantization A/B — target 2027-09-16 17:00 PDT (IN PROGRESS)
- Neha Kapoor: apply batch window change to canary group and report latency/throughput delta — 2027-09-15 12:00 PDT
- Monica Patel: stage prefix cache list and coordinate with MediLink team for top prompts — 2027-09-17
- Vivek Kulkarni: consolidate results and host exec readout (9/17) — 2027-09-17 14:00 PDT (proposed)

Attachments: llm-latency-run-20270913.csv; MAP-v2-MediLink.pdf; perf-dash-screenshots.zip

Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — performance benchmarking & close timeline (technical plan)

Adding the technical plan and expected deltas. Short version: the combination of KV prefetch + int8 quant profile should reduce p95 by 8–15% in our canary runs; throughput increases ~10% on average. Details below.

Planned tests (order + measurement points):
1) KV prefetch warmup: pre-warm KV for the top-200 prefixes at request start. Measurement: p95 over 10k requests across canary machines. Expected delta: -10–12% p95. Owner: Rafael — will run on 9/15 morning; results by 9/15 EOD.
2) Quantization A/B: int8 kernel with fp16 attention fallback for long sequences. Measurement: tokens/sec and mem consumption. Expected delta: +8–14% throughput; small tail risk for 32k+ sequences. Owner: Rafael — canary 9/16.
3) Batch window tightening (Neha): 40ms -> 25ms. Measurement: p50/p95 and overall tokens/sec. Expected delta: slight p50 improvement; throughput drop ~6%.
4) Canary rollout plan: start with 2 GPUs (same HW) -> expand to 8 -> full pool. Stop criteria: p95 increases >2% vs baseline or errors spike.

I’ll attach the canary run config and the perf dashboard link. If we hit p95 <= 220ms at canary step 2 we’re green for the Dedicated SLA.

Attachments: canary-config.yaml (referenced), perf-dash-screenshots.zip
